resources.string: Declarative modules (like a radio) can be installed from a signed file now.
Things you add to Abyss, like a radio. They show in Abyss under Apps. Anything that needs typing, like a server address, is set here.
A signed .abyssapp file, for example one built with a module\'s build.sh and copied to the phone.
Coming soon: adding a git repo as a source, kept up to date for you. Until then, build the module on a computer and install its .abyssapp file.
No file picker on this phone.
Version %1$s is installed; this installs it again.
Older version: %1$s is installed, this file is %2$s.
Signed by a different key than the installed version (%1$s). Remove the installed module first if you trust this file.
Same key as the installed version.
First install from this key. Install files only from people you trust: the signature says who made it, not that it is safe.
Changes are used from the next time you enter Abyss.
Abyss checked every file against the signature. It draws this module\'s screens and plays its audio itself; the addresses above are the only places it can reach.
Hold for one second with your finger.
Something is drawing over this screen. Close it, then hold again.
Hold it with your finger on the screen.
%1$s installed. In Abyss it is under Apps.
Keys are kept by Abyss\'s own key store, which isn\'t in this build yet, so this key can\'t be set yet.
Scripts and connectors you install all run as one Termux user, so any of them could read a key while it is in use. Install only scripts you trust.
This module isn\'t installed any more.
Saved. Used from the next time you enter Abyss.
New address: %1$s (on your home network). The module may only connect there after you allow it.
New address: %1$s, on the internet, not your home network. The module may only connect there after you allow it.
It goes from Abyss and its settings are deleted. Your captures stay.
